title: Documentation and Legal Ownership of Excavated Artefacts
what_it_is: Documentation and Legal Ownership of Excavated Artefacts

sections.label: NHB archaeological excavation requirements
sections.summary: NHB requires excavating agencies to document and report finds, accessions important materials into the National Collection, and typically lacks legal ownership of materials found on private land.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
sentences.text: When commissioning archaeological excavations, the National Heritage Board (NHB) makes it a requirement for the agencies conducting the excavation works, such as the Institute of Southeast Asian Studies (ISEAS)-Yusof Ishak Institute, to document and submit reports on the archaeological finds to NHB.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
sentences.text: Important archaeological materials from these digs that support the interpretation of Singapore's history have been accessioned into the National Collection managed by NHB on behalf of the Singapore Government.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
sentences.text: They are carefully documented and conserved at the Heritage Conservation Centre (HCC), when not on display.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
sentences.text: NHB typically does not have legal ownership of archaeological materials unearthed on private land.

sections.label: Review of archaeology laws
sections.summary: NHB is studying legal ownership of archaeological materials on private land as part of a broader review of archaeology in Singapore.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
sentences.text: The legal ownership status of archaeological materials unearthed on private land is an area that NHB is studying as part of a broader review on archaeology in Singapore.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
sentences.text: The review will seek to better support the conduct of archaeology in Singapore, and address any gaps in our laws, regulations and norms.

sections.label: Maritime archaeological finds support
sections.summary: Maritime archaeological finds are generally supported by MPA through the Merchant Shipping Act.

sentences.speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
sentences.text: On maritime archaeological finds, this is generally supported by the Maritime and Port Authority of Singapore (MPA) through the Merchant Shipping Act.

sections.label: Improving public archaeology engagement
sections.summary: The government is looking into improving laws and regulations to engage the interested public in cooperating with NHB on archaeology.

sentences.speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
sentences.text: With regard to the public, as I have answered earlier on, this is an area that we are looking further into.

sentences.speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
sentences.text: We are looking at how we should improve our laws and regulations to not discourage the public from having an interest, but to embrace and engage the public who are interested in archaeology to cooperate with NHB.
